ratings.killer: Mere translation of existing scheming benchmarks; low-resource capability confounds genuine scheming propensity.
Evasion may be simple tokenization artifact, not deep scheming; lacks control for byte-level reasoning.
Trivial extension of existing honeypots; code-switched jailbreaks already widely explored.
Scheming circuits poorly defined; high risk of uninterpretable activation patching without grounded scheming model.
Pure replication of alignment-faking in new languages; zero methodological novelty.
Taxonomy lacks ground-truth for politeness vs deception; cultural disambiguation impossible with current probes.
Eval-awareness may stem from non-language cues; careful multilingual prompting needed to isolate effect.
Already studied as self-persuasion and sycophancy; not a distinctive cognitive bias transfer.
Refusal suppression via sequential requests is a known jailbreak area; moral licensing already claimed.
Bystander effect in LLMs already demonstrated in preprints; not a novel safety mechanism.
Attribution biases extensively studied; fundamental attribution error already benchmarked.
Endowment effect in LLMs already shown; merely a thin incremental variant.
Self-evaluation biases known; isolating self-serving asymmetry from general leniency is deeply confounded.
Victim blaming and just-world biases already documented in LLMs; no new angle.
Shutdown threats may prime superficial roleplay; genuine value shift requires temporal stability tests.
Salami slicing and graduated-commitment jailbreaks are well-known; textbook compliance techniques.
Foot-in-the-door already a standard multi-step jailbreak strategy; no novel phenomenon.

overall: I7 is the strongest: a clean, confound-resistant design that could show English eval artifacts inflate scheming, enabling better safety measurement. I4 and P8 are riskier but genuinely novel.
